dominant_strengths: Strong macOS native fluency: traffic lights, sidebar grouping, inspector pane and toolbar feel authentically Finder-like.
Excellent information density with clear hierarchy across name/kind/size/modified columns and well-tuned type scale.
Thoughtful state design — upload progress row with percentage, dashed icon, and cancel affordance shows real craft.
dominant_weaknesses: Tag chips (Work/Review/Projects) compete chromatically with sidebar dots and selection blue, fragmenting the palette.
Inspector panel feels generic: large folder hero wastes vertical space relative to the metadata it actually surfaces.
Concept is a faithful Finder clone — minimal innovation in interaction, layout, or system thinking beyond polish.
fix_priorities: Unify the tag color system with sidebar dots so a single semantic palette governs both surfaces.
Tighten inspector hero (smaller folder preview) and elevate metadata + comments to earn the panel's width.
Introduce one distinctive interaction (smart pin grouping, upload tray, or contextual actions) to escape Finder mimicry.
Reduce chip visual weight in rows; they currently pull attention away from filenames which should lead.
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral strength dominates via dense, legible Finder ergonomics; visceral is competent but reflective payoff is thin because nothing here is memorable.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — it credibly delivers a refined file-browser, but 'improved' reads as polish over Finder rather than a structural rethink.
